items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Mutt Carey could sit on the bandstand and the Blackwood playing four hours. He could sit there and think of something, and before we leave there, he would play.

ctx.x: And then, Mutt Carey could sit on the bandstand and the Blackwood playing four hours. He could sit there and think of something, and before we leave there, he would play. You know, just get things together. He'd always come with something and he'd name it, just to give us some more funny name or something like that. And the people used to like it.
You mean he would think up a new tune and write on the bandstand?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: That's how Amos got with me once and Mutt got with me once when he left.

ctx.x: Oh, Solistan was in my lifetime playing first. You see, Solistan leaving my band and I didn't care where he would go, I'd always have open for him. When he come back, well he got ready to come back to the band and they all well understood that. They never did try to keep them out. You know, if he got out of the job he used to come right on back. But we started together and both of us was coming to boys and I kept the band going. He used to come right on back whenever he got ready. He left me about three or four…
Could you give me that picture of Thomas' man?
For the booking agent. For the group. For the group, really.

Now we are... Peter Ron never was a member of our band. Peter Booker was a member of our band. He played violin. Yeah. But at this time they make this picture. Peter Ron was a member of our band at that time. He never was. Now you're showing the name of your son of the cornet players? Oh yes. What do you mean? Louis Armstrong. Mark Carey. When did you work with Armstrong? Just... never was a member. But he jobbed around with us in Southern Standard Place at times. He was young. He was very young. He hadn't…
St. Sarah in the band, on the band, John?
